about: SCOPE AND BEHAVIOUR OF THE REFERENCES for insert-mode C-w and C-u, measured 2026-11-15 with oracle/run.py. busybox does NOT implement either command: char_insert() handles ESC, ^V, ^D, Backspace and Tab only, and do_cmd()'s insert branch forwards every byte >= 1 to char_insert, so the control byte is inserted LITERALLY - the buffer grows a \u0017 / \u0015. nvi implements both with vi-compatible semantics: it removes what the insert typed, never reaches past the insert start, and never joins a line (i.e. vim with backspace=""). vim is the behaviour oracle and is the superset implemented by this engine. This file exists so the gap is a MEASUREMENT rather than prose; it restricts itself to the pty engines, so the JS suites skip it and only `python3 oracle/run.py` runs it. ENGINES ARE THE PTY ONES ONLY: this file records what the references do, and the engine deliberately diverges from vim on the column-1 line join (docs/ENGINE.md), so including vim here would make our own suite assert a behaviour we have decided not to have. The `vim` expectation is kept per case as the reference column of the table in docs/ENGINE.md.

cases.name: busybox and nvi have no insert-mode C-w, so the byte lands in the buffer
vim deletes the word before the cursor
vim with nothing typed reaches back past the insert start; nvi cannot
vim clears the line when nothing was typed; nvi only removes what it typed
vim joins at column 1; nvi does not join at all
typed text is removed by every reference that implements the command
